hook: One lecture set math's agenda for a century

beats.say: In August 1900, at a math congress in Paris, David Hilbert gave a talk on the problems of the coming century. His friend Hermann Minkowski had urged him to look ahead.
He had time to read only ten aloud. The published version listed 23, from the nature of the infinite to the stacking of spheres.
Solving one became the surest way to make a name in mathematics, and whole fields grew up around single entries on the list.
